results.title: Over 80 brands await shoppers on final day of Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair at Ghud Park, Accra Mall
results.content: There is still time to shop, discover new brands and enjoy exciting offers at the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026, as the three-day exhibition enters its final day today, Sunday, November 15. If you have not visited yet, today is your last opportunity to make your way to Ghud Park at Accra Mall and experience an exhibition bringing together more than 80 brands from across Ghana. From food and beverages to fashion, beauty, agriculture, technology, finance, household products and real estate, visitors can explore a wide range of locally made products and services, meet business owners and take advantage of special deals and discounts.

results.title: NDC regional executive elections: The chairmen who retained their seats and those who lost
results.content: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has elected regional chairmen in 13 of Ghana’s 16 regions following its 2026 regional executive elections held on Saturday, November 14. Results from the Central, Oti and Savannah regions are still pending, with the Central Region contest yet to be formally declared. The elections produced notable changes in some regional leadership positions, while several incumbent chairmen retained their seats. In some regions, voting was delayed. In Ashanti, heightened security at the election centre meant voting had not started by early afternoon, although the contest was subsequently concluded.

results.title: NDC elects new Upper West chairman as four incumbents lose positions
results.content: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Upper West Region has elected procurement consultant Alhaji Alhassan Adam, popularly known as Randy, as its new Regional Chairman. The 49-year-old defeated incumbent chairman Abdul Nasir Saani Bunas, polling 196 votes against Bunas’ 164. Sombawiere Samba Sankara, immediate past Nadowli-Kaleo Constituency Chairman, received 28 votes. Randy’s victory marks a return to the contest after he lost to Bunas in the party’s 2022 regional elections. The elections, which involved 392 delegates and 63 aspirants, also saw four incumbent regional executives lose their positions.

results.title: Aviation professionals call for stronger training pathways for aspiring Ghanaian youth
results.content: Aviation professionals have called for stronger training opportunities and career guidance to prepare more young Ghanaians for employment in the aviation industry. They say while many young people aspire to become pilots, cabin crew members and other aviation professionals, limited access to information and structured training continues to make it difficult for some to navigate their way into the sector. The concerns were raised at the Take Off Experience, an initiative established by the founder of Global Aviation Consult, Ivy Hammond, to connect young people’s interest in aviation with practical guidance on entering the industry. Ms Hammond said she created the platform after observing that many aspiring professionals had ambitions but lacked the information and direction needed to pursue them.

results.title: The Price and promise of a solitary monetary policy
results.content: In 2025, the Bank of Ghana (BoG) accomplished something of extraordinary monetary significance. The cedi appreciated by 40.7 percent against the US dollar, its first annual gain in more than three decades and, on IMF data, the strongest performance of any African currency. Headline inflation, which had peaked at 54.1 percent in late 2022, fell to 5.4 percent by year-end, and gross international reserves rose to a record US$13.83 billion. The same year produced large losses on the Bank’s balance sheet. Its audited statements, released on 30 April 2026, show a net operating loss of GHS 15.63 billion, up from GHS 9.49 billion in 2024, and a further loss of GHS 19.32 billion in other comprehensive income. results.title: COP31: Two-thirds of Africa’s US$2.2bn clean cooking pledges yet to be delivered
results.content: Two years after leaders pledged US$2.2 billion to expand clean cooking in Africa, only about US$740 million has been paid out, leaving roughly two-thirds of the money, about US$1.46 billion, still to be delivered. The figures were presented at a Leaders’ Roundtable on Clean Cooking in Africa at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, on 12 November. The meeting was co-hosted by the COP31 Presidency of Türkiye, the United Republic of Tanzania, the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the Clean Cooking Alliance. The pledges were made at the first Summit on Clean Cooking in Africa, held in Paris in 2024 and co-chaired by Tanzania’s President Samia Suluhu Hassan. results.title: COP 31: Tanzania, Lesotho, Uganda share clean cooking gains as US$1.46bn in pledges is yet to arrive
results.content: Tanzania, Lesotho and Uganda have shared how they are expanding clean cooking at home, as leaders at COP31 warned that most of the money promised to help Africa make the switch is yet to arrive. The countries presented their progress at a Leaders’ Roundtable on Clean Cooking in Africa in Antalya, Türkiye, on 12 November, co-hosted by the COP31 Presidency of Türkiye, Tanzania, the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the Clean Cooking Alliance. Tanzania: from 16 to 35 per cent “I’m pleased to report that clean cooking access in Tanzania has increased from 16% in 2022,” President Samia Suluhu Hassan told the roundtable. She said access reached 28.6 per cent in March 2024 and is expected to hit 35 per cent by the end of 2026 (more than double in four years).

results.title: Daniel Niibi Afotey Odai elected NDC Greater Accra Deputy Youth Organiser
results.content: Daniel Niibi Afotey Odai has been elected Deputy Regional Youth Organiser of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Greater Accra Region after narrowly defeating three other contenders in the party’s regional executive elections. Niibi secured 45 votes in the election held on Saturday, November 14, 2026, edging his closest challenger, Atsu Eric Afeme, who polled 44 votes. Jones Klutse obtained 32 votes, while Rashid Isah secured eight. The result gives Niibi a new role in the party’s regional youth leadership as the NDC continues its internal reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general elections. Niibi’s political career began at the branch level. He served for eight years as Deputy Youth Organiser for the Krowor Constituency, where he was involved in youth mobilisation and organising party structures.

results.title: Sam Jonah credits Acheampong with advancing Ghanaian ownership of mineral wealth
results.content: Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has credited former Head of State General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong with advancing Ghanaian participation and ownership in the country’s mining and timber industries. Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Mr Jonah said Acheampong’s government introduced policies in 1972 that gave the state controlling interests in major companies, including Ashanti Goldfields and the Consolidated African Selection Trust. He said the measures were intended to increase Ghanaian control over the country’s natural resources while retaining foreign partners, their capital and technical expertise. “For the first time since the Portuguese landed at Elmina, the majority of the wealth beneath Ghanaian soil belonged to Ghanaians,” he said.

results.title: ArchXenus marks 15 years with more than 140 projects, launches GeneXus
results.content: Architecture firm ArchXenus has marked 15 years in practice with more than 140 projects, using its anniversary celebration to launch GeneXus, a book documenting 12 of its selected works, and to introduce initiatives aimed at strengthening its contribution to Ghana’s built environment. The two-day celebration, held on 10 and 11 November 2026 at Christ Temple East in Accra, a building ArchXenus designed and whose construction it managed, featured the launch of the GeneXus book, the Xenus Impact Foundation and the African Urban Futures Conclave. It also brought architects and other stakeholders together to examine the future of cities, climate-responsive buildings, housing and investment in the built environment. results.content: Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has criticised successive governments for abandoning the agricultural gains of General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong’s Operation Feed Yourself campaign, arguing that Ghana allowed a successful food production initiative to collapse. Delivering the Second General I.K. He said the campaign used radio broadcasts and information vans to encourage people across the country to participate in agricultural production. “Cutlasses, hoes, fertiliser and seed were sold at heavily subsidised prices. results.title: ‘Yentua’ was negotiation, not recklessness – Sam Jonah on Acheampong’s debt decision
results.content: Business leader Sam Jonah has praised former Head of State General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong’s 1972 decision to repudiate some of Ghana’s external debt, describing it as an act of courage and a demonstration of negotiation skill. Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Mr Jonah said Acheampong’s government announced on February 5, 1972, that Ghana would not honour about US$90 million in suppliers’ credits it considered tainted by corruption, fraud or inflated contracts. He said the decision became known through the Akan expression “Yentua”, meaning “we will not pay”. “The Daily Graphic put it in one Akan word, in a headline this country has never forgotten: Yentua. We will not pay,” he said.

results.title: Sam Jonah calls for honest reassessment of General I.K. Acheampong’s leadership
results.content: Business leader and University of Cape Coast Chancellor Sir Sam Jonah has called for a fresh and balanced examination of the leadership of former Head of State General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong, urging Ghanaians to confront the complexities of his time in office. Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture at the Marriott Hotel in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Sir Jonah said the country needed to move beyond the silence and polarised narratives surrounding the former military leader. He said the lecture offered an opportunity to examine Acheampong’s record, including his policies, achievements and shortcomings. “Our forebears left us a saying for an evening such as this: Se wo were fi na wosankofa a yenkyi. It is not wrong to go back for what you have forgotten. That is what we shall do tonight. We shall break the silence,” he said.
